liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (2 reviews): Peppy opening pairing that got things hopping immediately; Jerry stepped to the mic grinning and sang the first line; the crowd erupted [16][18]
- **Passenger** (1 review): Described as a rockin' version [7]
- **Sunrise** (1 review): Reviewer, not a Donna fan, found it tasty, and the crowd seemed to enjoy it [17]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Donna's singing here was judged weaker by the reviewer [17]
- **Drums** (1 review): Second-set jam flows into a nice mini melt leading to the drums [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-01-10.mtx.Rhinotrocity7.motb.95134.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 189 min; rated 4.78/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix sounds extremely crisp and clean; The soundboard runs fast and is very hissy from improper Dolby A; speed was adjusted to match the audience tape [1][16]
- **gd78-01-10.sbd.cotsman.14523.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 186 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Strong band sound on the soundboard, but microphone feedback squawks several times during the first two songs; This soundboard's quality is weaker than other circulating sources, though still worth hearing [7][9]
- **gd1978-01-10.aud.Rhinotrocity7.motb-0026.95068.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [5]. Said about its sound: A very sweet-sounding audience recording [11]
- **gd1978-01-10.133619.sbd.miller.flac24**: soundboard; 22 songs; 173 min [3]

## Around the show

- Garcia's first night singing after laryngitis; his vocals on the opener were understandably tentative [7]
- Garcia's voice was shot, yet the band still tore the Shrine up in the second set [9]
- Back at the Shrine, whose acoustics are praised; reviewer's first Passenger, Cassidy and Mexicali Blues [10]
- Early technical problems occurred, but the band sustained its energy through the show [16]
- Crowd buzzed over whether Jerry would sing, since Bobby handled vocals during the previous laryngitis-hit shows [18]
- The sizzling Other One is likened to the one at Market Square Arena [9]
- Reviewer found it less inspiring than the San Diego show [10]
- Rivals the Nashville Auditorium show as the best 1978 audience tape [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-01-10.mtx.Rhinotrocity7.motb.95134.flac16**: taped by Reinhart Hohlwein; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe and Adam Egert; source: Matrix (See Notes) [1]. Also: Audience taped with two AKG D224E microphones into a Sony TC 158, onto Maxell UDXL II cassettes; Cassettes transferred via Nakamichi CR7a and Korg MR-1000 to DSF, then AudioGate to 24/96 WAV [1]
- **gd78-01-10.sbd.cotsman.14523.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1978-01-10.aud.Rhinotrocity7.motb-0026.95068.flac16**: taped by Reinhart Hohlwein; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe and Adam Egert; source: 2 x AKG D224E's => Sony TC 158 >> MAC (3 x Maxell UDXL II) [5]. Also: Tape was stopped between every first-set song, with a flip during the drum solo; no patches applied; A separate matrix version adds crowd patches between songs and a drum solo patch [5]
- **gd1978-01-10.133619.sbd.miller.flac24**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Dolby B) -> FLAC (24bit/44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1978-01-11 Shrine Auditorium, Los Angeles, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1978-01-11-shrine-auditorium-los-angeles-ca-usa/) [20]
